summary: Removed the "intro" and "details" steps from the funnel, cutting it from 6 to 4 steps, because every extra step before email capture is a drop-off point — fewer friction steps between landing and email entry directly increases the share of visitors who complete signup.

Replaced the generic welcome headline and passive "Learn more" link with a benefit-focused headline, a bold "무료로 시작하기" (Start for free) CTA button, and reassurance copy ("30 seconds to sign up · cancel anytime") — removing ambiguity and friction at the top of the funnel drives more visitors to click through to step 1.

Added a green social-proof badge ("Already 12,000 people are with us ★★★★★") and three concrete benefit bullets (unlimited access, data security, and no-penalty cancellation) because social proof and explicit benefit specificity are the two highest-impact conversion levers when a page is otherwise vague — they address the visitor's "can I trust this?" and "what do I actually get?" hesitations before the click.
Removed the "verify" step from the funnel (4 steps → 3), eliminating the mid-flow email verification barrier that causes ~25% of users to abandon before completing signup.

Replaced the click-through CTA button with an inline email input form so users can enter their email directly on the landing page, eliminating one full page load and reducing funnel drop-off at the highest-traffic step.

Added a specific named testimonial (김민지, 직장인, 서울) directly above the signup form, because a concrete human quote with a name and context converts better than aggregate social proof alone — it makes the benefit feel real and personally relatable right at the moment of decision.
